spec.title: Flask-Driven Interactive Dashboard
spec.summary: A Flask application delivering a dynamic web dashboard with real-time data visualization, user filters, and responsive widgets. The front‑end renders charts via JavaScript, consuming RESTful endpoints exposed by Flask. The back‑end serves the index page, provides JSON data, and includes a test suite to ensure API stability.

files.name: app.py
files.purpose: Main Flask application initializing the web server, setting up API routes for dashboard data, handling CORS, and rendering the index template. Implements /api/stats endpoint returning JSON metrics and /api/filters for available filter options. Includes error handling middleware and a debug toggle.

files.name: requirements.txt
files.purpose: Lists all Python packages required to run the application, including Flask, Flask-RESTful, Flask-Cors for cross‑domain requests, pytest for testing, and requests for external API consumption.

files.name: templates/index.html
files.purpose: Server‑rendered HTML page containing the complete UI structure: header, navigation, chart containers, filter panels, and script tags linking to static JavaScript and CSS. Provides placeholders for dynamic content injected by static/app.js.

files.name: static/style.css
files.purpose: Cascading stylesheet defining layout, typography, and responsive grid for dashboard widgets, ensuring consistency across browsers and screen sizes. Styles navigation, chart containers, filter controls, and interactive hover states.

files.name: static/app.js
files.purpose: Client‑side JavaScript initializing charts using Chart.js, fetching data from Flask API endpoints, rendering interactive widgets, implementing filter controls, and updating the UI in real time with periodic refreshes. Handles loading indicators, error messages, and ensures responsiveness.

files.name: test_app.py
files.purpose: Pytest test suite validating Flask API endpoints: confirms 200 responses, correct JSON structure for /api/stats and /api/filters, checks for missing keys, and verifies no unhandled exceptions during request handling. Includes tests for application context and template rendering.

acceptance_criteria: GET / returns HTTP 200 and contains rendered index HTML
/api/stats endpoint returns JSON object with keys 'visits', 'sales', 'conversion'
/api/filters endpoint returns JSON array of filter options
Static JS loads correctly and renders at least one chart on page load
All tests in test_app.py pass without errors
assumptions_made: Assumed project type: interactive web dashboard
Assumed stack: Python Flask with HTML5 UI
